Use Case: Predict Trip Fares to Grow Revenue
Description: Predict Trip Fare from Route and Timing with Upfront Pricing Recommendations
Statement: Offering reliable upfront fares requires predicting fare_amount from route and timing before the trip completes, yet pricing currently depends on post-trip meter totals that cannot support quote-based products. This limits revenue from fixed-price offerings.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers features from trip_distance, pickup_zip, dropoff_zip and time-of-day/day-of-week derived from tpep_pickup_datetime, trains a Ridge regression (alpha tuned by cross-validation) to predict fare_amount, then uses ai_query to translate predicted fares into upfront quote recommendations.
Business Value: The Product Pricing Manager launches upfront fare quotes grounded in predicted fare_amount, aiming to increase booked-trip conversion and protect realized fare-per-mile [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Increase Revenue, Improve Customer Experience
Priority Reasons: A fare prediction model enables upfront quote products, a direct revenue opportunity, with the target fare_amount and all predictors present; conversion lift moves a revenue line.
Quality Reasons: Predictors trip_distance, pickup_zip, dropoff_zip and time-of-day/day-of-week from tpep_pickup_datetime train a cross-validated Ridge regression to estimate fare_amount before trip completion, producing a predicted_fare per route-time with residual evaluation. ai_query converts predictions into upfront quote recommendations, enabling the fixed-price product revenue outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Segment Pickup Zones to Improve Margins
Description: Segment Pickup Zones by Trip Economics with Pricing Zone Strategy
Statement: Pickup zones differ widely in trip distance, fare levels and trip duration, but without data-driven grouping the pricing team treats all zones uniformly, leaving margin opportunities on the table. Zone-level economics are hidden in raw fare_amount and trip_distance distributions.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates per-zone features from pickup_zip, fare_amount, trip_distance and durations from tpep_pickup_datetime/tpep_dropoff_datetime, runs K-Means clustering to group zones into economic segments, then uses ai_query to recommend a pricing posture per segment.
Business Value: The Pricing Manager assigns a differentiated pricing posture per zone segment, aiming to increase average fare_amount per trip in under-monetized zones and protect volume in price-sensitive ones [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Priority Reasons: Zone economic segmentation directly supports differentiated pricing posture that lifts average fare in under-monetized zones, moving a revenue line computable from per-zone fare_amount aggregates.
Quality Reasons: Per-zone features from pickup_zip, fare_amount, trip_distance and durations (tpep_pickup_datetime/tpep_dropoff_datetime) are aggregated into fare-per-mile, dispersion and avg-duration metrics, standardized, then clustered with K-Means (k by silhouette) to produce zone economic segments. ai_query maps segments to a pricing posture, delivering the per-zone fare-increase outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Forecast Trip Demand to Reduce Idle Cost
Description: Forecast Trip Demand by Pickup Zone with Fleet Positioning Recommendations
Statement: Fleet utilization suffers when vehicles sit idle in low-demand zones while high-demand zones go underserved, measurable through hourly trip counts derived from tpep_pickup_datetime and pickup_zip. Without forward-looking demand signals the operations team cannot pre-position vehicles.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates trip counts by pickup_zip and hourly buckets from tpep_pickup_datetime, fits a Prophet time-series model per zone with calendar and hour-of-day features, then uses ai_query to translate zone-level forecasts into pre-positioning recommendations.
Business Value: The Fleet Operations Manager re-positions vehicles each shift using the forecast, aiming to increase served-trip volume (count of rows per pickup_zip) and reduce idle time between trips [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_pickup_datetime].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Increase Revenue, Reduce Cost, Improve Customer Experience, Boost Productivity
Priority Reasons: Zone-level demand forecasting from pickup timestamp and zip supports pre-positioning that lifts served-trip volume and reduces idle time, moving both revenue and cost lines computable from row counts per zone.
Quality Reasons: Demand signal carried by tpep_pickup_datetime and pickup_zip; aggregating COUNT(*) into hourly buckets per zone yields a trips_per_zone_hour series. Engineering hour-of-day, day-of-week and lag features feeds a per-zone Prophet forecast, producing a projected_demand KPI per zone-hour. Translating forecasts to shift pre-positioning directly serves the fleet utilization and served-trip volume outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_pickup_datetime].

Use Case: Detect Fare Irregularities to Protect Revenue
Description: Detect Fare Irregularities per Distance with Investigation Queue
Statement: Trips where fare_amount is inconsistent with trip_distance can indicate meter errors, fare manipulation or data-entry faults that erode revenue integrity. These irregularities are invisible in simple totals.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers per-trip features from fare_amount, trip_distance and trip duration computed from tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime, trains an Isolation Forest to flag outlier trips, then uses ai_query to explain each flagged trip and route it to the correct review team.
Business Value: The Revenue Assurance Analyst works a daily queue of flagged trips, aiming to recover revenue tied to under-billed trips and reduce the count of anomalous fare_amount values [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Priority Reasons: Isolation Forest on fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute flags under-billed or manipulated trips, feeding a daily recovery queue that moves a revenue-integrity line computable from fare_amount.
Quality Reasons: Anomaly signal from fare_amount against trip_distance plus duration derived from tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime; computing fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute ratios feeds an Isolation Forest (contamination=0.03) that scores each trip, yielding an anomaly_score per trip. Routing flagged outliers to an investigation queue directly enables the revenue recovery outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Identify Low-yield Trips to Protect Margins
Description: Identify Unprofitable Long-Distance Trips with Route Pricing Corrections
Statement: Some long-distance trips return low fare_amount relative to trip_distance and elapsed duration, dragging down effective yield, but these low-yield trips are not separated from healthy ones in reporting. Uncorrected, they erode margin on every repeat.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code derives fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute from fare_amount, trip_distance, tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime, trains a Random Forest classifier to label trips as low-yield versus healthy using corridor features from pickup_zip/dropoff_zip, then uses ai_query to recommend route-level pricing corrections.
Business Value: The Yield Management Analyst targets corridors generating recurring low-yield trips, aiming to raise effective fare-per-mile and reduce the share of trips classified as low-yield [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Priority Reasons: Labeling low-yield corridors feeds route pricing corrections that lift effective fare-per-mile, directly moving yield, a revenue/margin line computable from fare_amount and trip_distance.
Quality Reasons: Yield signal from fare_amount, trip_distance and duration (tpep_pickup_datetime/tpep_dropoff_datetime) yields fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute; a Random Forest classifier using pickup_zip/dropoff_zip corridor features labels trips low-yield vs healthy, producing a low_yield_share KPI per corridor. ai_query recommends corridor pricing corrections, delivering the yield-improvement outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Forecast Revenue Peaks to Grow Revenue
Description: Forecast Hourly Revenue to Anticipate Peak Earnings Windows with Driver Incentive Plan
Statement: Revenue intensity concentrates in specific hourly windows, but without a forward revenue forecast the incentives team cannot time driver bonuses to the highest-yield periods, leaving peak demand under-supplied. Realized fare_amount per hour varies sharply.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates summed fare_amount into hourly buckets from tpep_pickup_datetime, fits an ai_forecast time-series model with hour and weekday seasonality, then uses ai_query to recommend when to deploy driver incentives for peak earnings windows.
Business Value: The Driver Incentives Manager schedules bonus windows around forecast revenue peaks, aiming to increase total fare_amount captured during peak hours and lift driver availability when it matters most [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Increase Revenue, Boost Productivity
Priority Reasons: Hourly revenue forecasting times driver incentives to peak windows, lifting fare captured and availability when it matters, a revenue line computable from summed fare_amount per hour.
Quality Reasons: Revenue signal from fare_amount summed into hourly buckets off tpep_pickup_datetime; engineering hour-of-day and weekday seasonal features feeds an ai_forecast model producing a projected_hourly_revenue series. ai_query places incentive windows on forecast peaks, directly serving the peak-earnings capture outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Detect Slow Trips to Protect Revenue
Description: Detect Abnormally Slow Trips for Equivalent Routes with Service Alert Queue
Statement: Trips covering similar distances between the same pickup and dropoff zones sometimes take far longer than peers, signaling congestion, detours, or meter issues that erode trip throughput and rider trust. Flagging these outliers lets operations investigate systemic route problems.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code groups trips by pickup_zip and dropoff_zip, computes trip duration from tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime normalized by trip_distance, trains an Isolation Forest on duration-per-mile and distance features to flag outlier trips, then uses ai_query to explain each flagged trip and generate an investigation alert.
Business Value: The Service Quality Lead works a ranked alert queue of abnormally slow trips, targeting a reduction in excess duration-per-mile derived from tpep_pickup_datetime, tpep_dropoff_datetime and trip_distance [ESTIMATE: depends on trip_distance].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Improve Customer Experience, Boost Productivity
Priority Reasons: Flagging slow trips per zone pair targets throughput and rider trust, an efficiency and quality KPI whose revenue effect is indirect; still a defensible always-on alert queue.
Quality Reasons: Signal from duration (tpep_dropoff_datetime minus tpep_pickup_datetime) normalized by trip_distance within pickup_zip/dropoff_zip peer groups; computing duration-per-mile per zone pair feeds an Isolation Forest with hour-of-day context, yielding a slowness anomaly_score per trip. Ranking flagged outliers into a service alert queue drives the throughput and route-issue investigation outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on trip_distance].

Use Case: Forecast Trip Duration to Improve Satisfaction
Description: Forecast Zone Pair Trip Duration with Rider Wait Time Communication Plan
Statement: Expected travel time between zone pairs shifts by hour and day, and inaccurate estimates frustrate riders and complicate dispatch promises. Forecasting duration per zone pair and time window supports reliable arrival estimates and better rider communication.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates trip duration (from tpep_pickup_datetime to tpep_dropoff_datetime) by pickup_zip, dropoff_zip and time bucket, fits a time-series forecast with calendar features from the pickup timestamp, then uses ai_query to explain duration drivers and recommend rider wait-time messaging per corridor.
Business Value: The Customer Experience Manager sets corridor-level arrival estimates, aiming to reduce the error between promised and actual duration derived from tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_dropoff_datetime].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Improve Customer Experience
Priority Reasons: Zone-pair duration forecasting improves arrival estimates and rider communication, a customer-experience KPI whose revenue effect is indirect but a defensible recurring forecast.
Quality Reasons: Duration signal from tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime aggregated by pickup_zip/dropoff_zip and hourly/day-of-week bucket; fitting Prophet or ai_forecast with calendar features produces a projected_duration per corridor-time. ai_query turns forecasts into rider wait-time messaging, serving the arrival-estimate accuracy outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_dropoff_datetime].

Use Case: Identify Top Trip Corridors to Grow Revenue
Description: Reveal Revenue Concentration Across Trip Corridors with Corridor Investment Plan
Statement: A small share of pickup-to-dropoff corridors likely drives a disproportionate share of total fare_amount, but the commercial team lacks visibility into which pickup_zip to dropoff_zip corridors concentrate revenue. Spreading investment evenly wastes effort.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code groups trips by the pickup_zip and dropoff_zip corridor pair, sums fare_amount and trip counts, applies a Pareto ranking to find the vital-few corridors, then uses ai_query to recommend where to concentrate driver supply and promotion.
Business Value: The Commercial Strategy Lead focuses supply and promotional spend on the vital-few corridors, aiming to grow total fare_amount captured on high-yield corridors while trimming effort on long-tail routes [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Priority Reasons: Pareto ranking of corridors by summed fare concentrates supply and promotion on the vital-few, directly moving revenue captured on high-yield corridors, computable from fare_amount by corridor.
Quality Reasons: Corridor key built from pickup_zip and dropoff_zip; aggregating SUM(fare_amount) and COUNT per corridor yields revenue_per_corridor, and cumulative revenue share produces a Pareto ranking identifying the vital-few corridors. ai_query turns the ranked list into a corridor investment plan, directly serving the revenue-concentration outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Optimize Surge Pricing to Grow Revenue
Description: Simulate Zone-Based Surge Pricing Impact with Revenue Optimization Recommendations
Statement: Fare per mile and demand vary sharply by zone and hour, and uniform pricing leaves revenue uncaptured in high-demand windows while risking lost volume in weak ones. Simulating pricing scenarios per zone and time window quantifies the revenue trade-off.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds zone-hour demand and fare profiles from fare_amount, trip_distance, pickup_zip and tpep_pickup_datetime, runs Monte Carlo simulations of fare multiplier scenarios against modeled demand response, then uses ai_query to explain scenario outcomes and recommend an optimal pricing schedule per zone.
Business Value: The Pricing Manager selects zone-hour pricing scenarios, aiming to increase total fare captured in fare_amount while controlling trip volume [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Priority Reasons: Monte Carlo surge simulation targets total fare captured, a direct revenue lever, but demand elasticity is an assumption the dataset cannot estimate, so the simulation leans on modeled parameters not grounded in the schema.
Quality Reasons: Zone-hour profiles from fare_amount, trip_distance, pickup_zip and tpep_pickup_datetime give observed demand and fare-per-mile per zone-hour; Monte Carlo over fare-multiplier scenarios projects a revenue_outcome distribution. ai_query recommends an optimal zone-hour schedule, serving the revenue optimization outcome, though the elasticity response is an assumed parameter not derivable from the schema [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].

Use Case: Detect Demand Shifts to Reduce Cost
Description: Detect Shifting Demand Patterns Across Time of Day with Scheduling Adjustments
Statement: Trip volume and fare intensity vary across hours and days, and gradual shifts in these patterns can leave shifts over- or under-staffed, inflating idle cost or lost trips. These drifts are not visible in static schedules.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds hour-of-day and day-of-week trip-count and fare_amount series from tpep_pickup_datetime, applies STL decomposition to separate trend from seasonality and detect sustained level shifts, then uses ai_query to recommend concrete shift-schedule adjustments.
Business Value: The Workforce Planning Lead rebalances shift coverage to match detected demand trends, aiming to reduce idle hours and the count of unserved high-demand periods [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_pickup_datetime].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Reduce Cost, Boost Productivity
Priority Reasons: STL decomposition of hourly trip and fare series surfaces sustained demand drifts that drive staffing rebalancing, improving an efficiency KPI (idle hours and unserved periods) whose money effect is one step removed.
Quality Reasons: Temporal signal from tpep_pickup_datetime with fare_amount builds hourly/daily trip-count and fare-intensity series. STL decomposition separates trend from seasonality to flag sustained level shifts, producing a demand_drift metric per time bucket. Converting flagged shifts into shift-schedule adjustments drives the idle-hour reduction outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_pickup_datetime].

Use Case: Classify Trip Profiles to Improve Efficiency
Description: Classify Trips as Short-Haul or Long-Haul Behavior with Fleet Mix Planning Actions
Statement: The operation serves distinct trip profiles (quick intra-zone hops versus long cross-city runs) that demand different vehicle positioning and driver shift planning. Classifying trips by behavioral profile clarifies the service mix and informs fleet allocation.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers features from trip_distance, fare_amount, trip duration and zone transition between pickup_zip and dropoff_zip, trains a Random Forest classifier to assign each trip a haul-profile label, then uses ai_query to explain profile share by zone and recommend fleet mix actions.
Business Value: The Fleet Planning Manager adjusts vehicle allocation by profile mix per zone, aiming to improve revenue-per-mile in fare_amount relative to trip_distance across the fleet [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Reduce Cost, Boost Productivity
Priority Reasons: Haul-profile classification informs fleet mix, improving revenue-per-mile indirectly, but short vs long haul is essentially a distance threshold, so a trained classifier adds limited incremental decision value over a rule.
Quality Reasons: Features from trip_distance, fare_amount, duration (from tpep_pickup_datetime and tpep_dropoff_datetime) and the pickup_zip to dropoff_zip transition feed a Random Forest to assign a haul-profile label per trip, producing a profile_share KPI by zone. Aggregating fare-per-mile by profile and zone surfaces where fleet mix should shift, supporting the revenue-per-mile outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
